chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife, so she became independent from him, and she had a daughter who was a slave-girl, and he bought her. Is it permissible for him to have intercourse with her? He said, 'No.'.

As for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Razin, the seller of fabrics, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'A man had a slave-girl, he had intercourse with her, then he sold her or she died, then he found her daughter. Is he permitted to have intercourse with her?' He said, 'Yes. Allah has forbidden this only from the free women, but as for the slave-girls, there is no harm.'.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry the daughter of his former slave-girl after divorcing her?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the juristic distinction between free women (*hur*) and slave-girls (*im'*) regarding the prohibition of *mahram* relationships through marriage or intercourse. While the primary narration from Imam al-Sadiq prohibits a man from marrying the daughter of his former slave-girl after her sale or divorce, the secondary narration from Imam al-Jawad clarifies that the divine prohibition specifically targets free women, thereby permitting relations with slave-girls. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the status of the mother determining the specific nature of the prohibition in cases of manumission or sale.
